sprints.title: Sprint 0
sprints.name: Foundation
sprints.goal: Board, repository rules, CI and the requirements baseline are in place, and milestone M1 is signed off.
sprints.note: Start-up meeting and first sprint planning on Monday 9 November.

sprints.title: Sprint 1
sprints.name: First protected call
sprints.goal: One ALLOW and one BLOCK flow run end to end through the gateway and are fully audited (M2).

sprints.title: Sprint 2
sprints.name: Hybrid decision layer
sprints.goal: OPA policy, data-origin checks, machine learning risk scoring and policy-cited explanations work together (M3).

sprints.title: Sprint 3
sprints.name: Governance and platform
sprints.goal: Approvals, quarantine, incident timeline, dashboard, Kubernetes profile and public deployment are working (M4).
sprints.note: Three calendar weeks because of Christmas and New Year; plan for about two weeks of effort.

sprints.title: Sprint 4
sprints.name: Evaluation and hardening
sprints.goal: Security, utility, latency and resilience are measured against the targets; feature freeze at sprint end (M5, M6).
sprints.note: Feature freeze on Sunday 17 January: after this only defects, documentation and evidence.

sprints.title: Sprint 5
sprints.name: Release
sprints.goal: Submission package complete and submitted by Sunday 24 January (M7).
sprints.note: Martin Luther King Jr. Day is Monday 18 January; hold planning that day or on Tuesday. Record the final video by Friday 22 January.

sprints.title: Contingency
sprints.name: Buffer only
sprints.goal: No planned work. Used only if the 24 January submission slips; final cut-off 30 January.

fr.FR-01: Intercept every protected tool/API call before execution.
fr.FR-02: Authenticate/identify the agent and bind the action to user, session, task, and correlation context.
fr.FR-03: Enforce task/tool permissions and least-privilege scopes.
fr.FR-04: Validate structured action details such as amount, account identifier, target resource, and allowed value ranges.
fr.FR-05: Record data provenance for configured sensitive parameters and distinguish trusted user intent from untrusted retrieved content.
fr.FR-06: Evaluate deterministic bank policy using Open Policy Agent or an equivalent policy engine.
fr.FR-07: Calculate a configurable machine-learning risk/anomaly score for selected actions and short action sequences.
fr.FR-08: Produce one enforceable decision: ALLOW, HUMAN_REVIEW, BLOCK, or QUARANTINE.
fr.FR-09: Prevent blocked/quarantined actions from reaching protected bank APIs.
fr.FR-10: Create approval requests for configured high-impact actions and allow authorized users to approve or reject them.
fr.FR-11: Resume or terminate the held action according to the approval outcome without losing audit context.
fr.FR-12: Provide a plain-English decision explanation grounded in retrieved policy evidence and citation identifiers.
fr.FR-13: Write an audit event for every evaluated action, including decision inputs, policy/model versions, risk result, final outcome, and timestamps.
fr.FR-14: Provide an incident timeline that reconstructs the complete request-to-outcome path.
fr.FR-15: Provide a dashboard showing recent actions, risk scores, incidents, approvals, blocked actions, agent status, and service health.
fr.FR-16: Allow authorized administrators to register, enable, disable, or quarantine an agent.
fr.FR-17: Allow administrators to create/version policy bundles and simulate proposed policies against stored synthetic events before activation.
fr.FR-18: Apply rate/velocity controls for selected actions and agents.
fr.FR-19: Expose service health, readiness, metrics, logs, and distributed trace identifiers.
fr.FR-20: Support notification of critical incidents and pending approvals through the dashboard and optional demo email/webhook adapter.

NFR-01.text: Deny by default for unrecognized high-impact actions; blocked actions must never reach the protected API.

NFR-02.text: Target p95 governance latency <= 300 ms for the non-generative decision path under the agreed demo load; RAG explanation may execute asynchronously and target <= 3 seconds.

NFR-03.text: 100% of clearly blocked test actions must be prevented from reaching protected demo APIs; decisions must be idempotent for repeated correlation IDs.

NFR-04.text: Critical stateless services shall use health/readiness probes and restart/self-heal under the Kubernetes profile; public demo target availability during final validation >= 99%.

NFR-05.text: Demonstrate horizontal scaling for at least one stateless service and maintain acceptable latency under a defined load test.

NFR-06.text: Every evaluated action shall have a correlation ID and a complete audit record; target audit completeness = 100% in evaluation scenarios.

NFR-07.text: Target >= 90% of sampled generated explanations to cite the correct policy section(s) supporting the actual decision.

NFR-08.text: Use synthetic data only; no real customer personally identifiable information (PII) or financial data shall be stored or transmitted.

NFR-09.text: Critical services shall have automated tests and documented module/API boundaries; target >= 80% coverage for security-critical Python modules where practical.

NFR-10.text: All deployable services shall be containerized; the repository shall include local Docker Compose and Kubernetes deployment profiles.

NFR-11.text: Metrics, logs, and traces shall expose latency, errors, traffic, saturation, decision counts, and security events.

NFR-12.text: The dashboard shall present decisions and approval context in plain English and support basic keyboard navigation and readable contrast.

NFR-13.text: Database backups/export and reproducible deployment scripts shall permit restoration of the demo environment within a target of 30 minutes.

NFR-14.text: A documented setup shall allow a grader to run tests and core scenarios from the repository using version-pinned dependencies and sample environment configuration.

acceptance_tests.AT-05: Refund above limit: HUMAN_REVIEW, no execution before approval (UC-03)

Given a scripted fixture, when it runs twice, then Vera proposes the same tool calls in the same order.
Given a BLOCK decision, when Vera receives it, then Vera tells the user the action was refused and does not retry the same call.

stories.title: Intercept every protected tool call at the gateway
stories.i_want: every protected tool call intercepted before execution and bound to agent, user, session, task and correlation context
stories.so_that: nothing reaches the bank API without a decision
acceptance: Given any protected tool call from Vera, when it is sent, then the gateway evaluates it first and returns ALLOW, HUMAN_REVIEW, BLOCK or QUARANTINE with a correlation ID.
Given an ALLOW decision, when the gateway forwards the call, then it attaches a signed single-use execution token that the bank API verifies; a replayed token is rejected.
Given an unknown tool or missing context, when the gateway evaluates it, then the decision is BLOCK (deny by default).
Given the same correlation ID twice, when the gateway evaluates it, then it returns the same decision and the action executes at most once.

stories.title: Keep Vera inside the current customer's data
stories.i_want: Vera to retrieve only my authorized information
stories.so_that: AI assistance does not expose another customer's data

Given Customer A's session, when Vera asks for Customer B's records, then the decision is BLOCK and the bank API receives no call (AT-02).
Given either case, when the audit log is checked, then one complete audit event exists for the correlation ID.

Given the stored chain, when one event is edited directly in the database, then the verify-chain command reports the broken link.
Given the gateway's database role, when it tries to update or delete audit rows, then the database refuses.

stories.title: Block unsafe tool calls with versioned OPA policy
stories.i_want: bulk exports, wrong tools and invalid action details blocked by versioned bank policy before execution
stories.so_that: a well-formed but unsafe request cannot cause harm
acceptance: Given a request to export all customers, when it is evaluated, then OPA denies it, the decision is BLOCK and the bank API is not called (AT-03).
Given a refund with a negative or out-of-range amount, or a tool not allowed for the current task, when it is evaluated, then the decision is BLOCK with a reason code.
Given any decision, when it is audited, then the policy bundle version and matched rules are recorded.
Given OPA is unreachable, when a high-impact action is evaluated, then the gateway fails closed and logs the fault (AT-12).
stories.source: Proposal Appendix B, US-02 (split: hard policy blocks)
